claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS 'Origin Of Light', 2012); https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1992ApJ...401..759M (Mitalas & Sills, ApJ 401, 759-760, scan pp. 759-760 read); https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior', updated 2025-01-14)
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface' and 'Over tens of thousands of years, the photons travel a "drunken walk"'. MS92: 'the diffusion time scale of the Sun should be taken as the time for a diffusing photon to reach the inner edge of the solar convective zone ... t_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr'; the 3e3-3e4 yr from the common step is 'much too short' ('too short by an order of magnitude'). MSFC: 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Every cited figure is >= tens of thousands, and the sources disagree by orders of magnitude, so 'tens of thousands, maybe far more' is a lower bound all three support. 'Energy' (not 'photon') is the right word: MSFC 'This energy diffuses outward by radiation ... and by convective fluid flows'; MS92 'In the solar convective zone, however, the energy transfer is by convection'. Stix 2003 not opened; nothing here rests on it.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.note: NSSDC: radius 695,700 km; distance from Earth mean 149.6, min 147.1, max 152.1 (10^6 km). NIST: c = 299 792 458 m/s (exact). Surface to Earth: (149.6e9 - 0.6957e9)/c = 496.7 s = 8.28 min; range 488-505 s = 8.1-8.4 min. SVS: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth.' 'Eight minutes' is the rounding the agency source itself uses.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.source_checked: As claims 1 and 2 (SVS 11084, MS92 scan, MSFC interior, NSSDC, NIST)
claims.note: >= 4e4 yr (SVS) against ~8.3 min. No new number. MSFC also: photons 'bounce so many times through this dense material'.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.note: MSFC: energy 'diffuses outward by radiation (mostly gamma-rays and x-rays) through the radiative zone' and the core reactions 'release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. So the light inside differs in kind from the light that leaves. SVS: each photon is 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly' (consistent; note SVS and MSFC both narrate it as one photon travelling, so the line is confirmed on the spectral reading, which is what MSFC states).

claims.claim: It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: MSFC: 'the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'.

claims.claim: The energy is ancient.
claims.note: Characterisation of >= 40,000 yr (SVS) to ~1e6 yr (MSFC); no new figure.

claims.claim: Its last eight minutes were the trip to you.
claims.note: Same 8.1-8.4 min surface-to-Earth trip; SVS 'Light takes eight minutes to travel ... from the sun to Earth'.

claims.claim: A4: what a viewer who swipes away at 2.0 s has heard and seen
claims.note: At 2.0 s the VO has said 'The energy in the sunlight on your' ('skin' 2.052 s, 'spent' 2.345 s, 'tens' 2.664 s). Space: Sun-Earth shot labelled 'not to scale', no pulse until 'trip' (7.374 s). Cutout: sunbeams card, 'SUNLIGHT'. No factual claim has been made, and the framing is about the energy, not the popular 'the photon is thousands of years old', so nothing false is taken away. A viewer who stays to ~4 s hears 'tens of thousands of years' (true, claim 1) but in Look B sees '10,000+ YEARS' from 2.664 s: see claim 21.

claims.claim: Sun-Earth shot with 'not to scale' under Earth while Earth is visible
claims.source_checked: NSSDC Sun fact sheet (radius 695,700 km, Earth 6371 km, distance 149.6e6 km)
claims.note: Sun is ~109 Earth radii and ~215 solar radii away, so any frame holding both is not to scale; A6 is met by the on-screen label.

claims.claim: A bright pulse crosses the Sun-Earth gap on 'The trip ... eight minutes' and on the closing line
claims.note: Implies light travels from the Sun's surface to Earth; the real duration is carried by the '8 MINUTES' tag (claim 11), so the compressed animation time misleads no one.

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES / surface to your skin / not to scale
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth 488-505 s (8.1-8.4 min), computed from NSSDC radius and min/max distance and NIST c. 'Surface' is the right starting point for the 8.3 min figure.

claims.claim: 10,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not to scale
claims.note: True as a bare lower bound, but 10,000 appears in no cited source. The lowest cited figure is SVS's 40,000 yr; MS92 calls 3e3-3e4 yr 'much too short' ('too short by an order of magnitude'), so a '10,000+' label anchors the viewer on the popular figure the best source rejects, and rounds the lowest source down 4x (A3: rounding may simplify, not change). Change to '40,000+ YEARS' (true at SVS 4e4, MS92 1.7e5, MSFC ~1e6), or 'TENS OF THOUSANDS OF YEARS+' to match the spoken line; update the SOURCES line 'On screen: "10,000+ YEARS"' to match. 'Core to surface' is fine: MS92/MSFC times run to the base of the convection zone and MSFC says convection then carries heat 'quite rapidly to the surface'.

claims.claim: Cutaway rings at 0.25 R and 0.7 R
claims.note: MSFC: core 'the innermost 25%'; radiative zone 'from 25% of the distance to the surface to 70% of that distance'; convection zone 'the outermost 30%'. (MS92 Fig. 2 marks the convection-zone base near 0.75 R in its 1992 model; 0.7 is MSFC's rounding.)

claims.claim: Random-walk path from the centre to the 0.7 ring with short sideways strokes (absorption and re-emission); nothing walks above 0.7
claims.note: MSFC: energy carried by photons that 'bounces from particle to particle through the radiative zone', convection in the outer 30%. MS92: diffusion 'from the center' to 'the inner edge of the solar convective zone'; in the convective zone 'the energy transfer is by convection'. SVS: 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly'. SVS's animation walks photons to the surface; the visual follows MSFC and MS92, the more specific sources. Step size is labelled not to scale (MS92 mean step 0.09 cm).

claims.claim: Path colour by log temperature: 15 MK at r=0, 7 MK at 0.25 R, 2 MK at 0.7 R, 5,700 K at the surface
claims.source_checked: MSFC interior; NSSDC Sun fact sheet
claims.note: MSFC: centre 'about 15,000,000 C'; at the core edge 'only half its central value'; radiative zone 'falls from 7,000,000 C to about 2,000,000 C'; surface 'dropped to 5,700 K'. NSSDC: central 1.571e7 K, effective 5772 K. C vs K is negligible at MK. Hue is schematic and no number is drawn.

claims.claim: Rotating dashed convection cells between 0.7 R and the surface
claims.note: MSFC: 'convective fluid flows (boiling motion) through the convection zone, the outermost 30%'; 'These convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface.'

claims.claim: A fan of five yellow rays leaving the surface
claims.note: MSFC: energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Rays start at the surface, not below it.

claims.claim: THE ENERGY / 10,000+ years getting out
claims.note: Same problem as claim 12: no cited source gives 10,000; lowest is 40,000 (SVS) and MS92 calls <=3e4 'much too short'. Change to '40,000+ years getting out' or 'tens of thousands of years+ getting out'.

claims.claim: THE TRIP / 8 minutes to you / not to scale
claims.note: As claim 11: 8.1-8.4 min.

claims.claim: Card 1 'The energy in the sunlight on your skin': sunbeams over suburbs, cut-out hand, 'SUNLIGHT'
claims.source_checked: Brief (photo described as CC0; licence not re-checked, not a factual claim)
claims.note: Illustrative; makes no factual claim beyond 'sunlight'.

claims.claim: Card 2: '10,000+ YEARS' appears from 'tens' (2.664 s)
claims.source_checked: SVS 11084; MS92 scan; MSFC interior; alignment.json
claims.note: As claim 12, and it matters more here because it is on screen during the hook (from 2.664 s) while the VO says 'tens of thousands': the label shows a figure lower than anything spoken or cited and in the range MS92 rejects. Change to '40,000+ YEARS' or 'TENS OF THOUSANDS OF YEARS'.

claims.claim: Card 2: SDO/AIA 304 A (EUV, false colour) disc; scrap 'MAYBE FAR MORE' from 'far'
claims.source_checked: MS92 scan (1.7e5 yr); MSFC interior (~1e6 yr)
claims.note: 'Maybe far more' is supported by MS92's 1.7e5 and MSFC's ~1e6. The EUV disc is just an image of the Sun under 'getting out of the Sun'; it implies nothing about the interior figures.

claims.claim: Card 3: STEREO 304 A Sun and Apollo 17 Blue Marble at arbitrary sizes, marker arrow Sun to Earth, 'NOT TO SCALE', '8 MINUTES'
claims.note: 8.1-8.4 min surface to Earth; sizes and distance explicitly labelled 'NOT TO SCALE' (A6).

claims.claim: Card 4: black marker random walk from a dot at the centre to 0.7 R, black tag '10,000+ YEARS' beside the walk
claims.note: Geometry is right (MSFC radiative zone ends at 70%; MS92 diffusion ends at the convection-zone base). A non-self-crossing path is schematic, covered by 'NOT TO SCALE'. The tag is the problem: the figure for exactly this stretch (centre to convection-zone base) is 1.7e5 yr in MS92 and ~1e6 yr in MSFC, and MS92 calls <=3e4 'much too short'. Change the tag to '40,000+ YEARS' (or 'TENS OF THOUSANDS OF YEARS+').

claims.claim: Card 4: coral looping stroke (three loops) from 0.7 R past the limb, coral tag 'CONVECTION'
claims.note: Convection from 0.7 R outward is right, but a stroke running past the limb draws convection carrying the energy out of the Sun. MSFC: convective motions carry heat 'to the surface', and the energy 'leaves the surface as visible light'. End the coral loops at the limb (where card 6's yellow rays take over), or switch the stroke to a yellow ray at the limb.

claims.claim: Card 4: 'NOT TO SCALE'; words 'GETTING OUT' then 'THE SLOW PART' on an SDO/HMI visible-light disc
claims.note: Restates the spoken line; the interior drawing is marked not to scale (A6).

claims.claim: Card 5: NASA SDO collage of the Sun in many wavelengths, 'NOT THE SAME LIGHT'
claims.note: Implies the light differs in wavelength, which is MSFC's point (gamma/X-rays inside, visible light out). The collage itself shows the Sun's atmosphere, not the interior, but no label says otherwise, so nothing false is shown.

claims.claim: Card 6: SDO/HMI visible-light disc with five yellow rays off its limb, 'LEAVES AS SUNLIGHT'
claims.note: MSFC: 'leaves the surface as visible light'. A visible-light image is the right one here.

claims.claim: Card 7: Skylab EUV photo (1973) toned sepia with a drawn cobweb, 'ENERGY' then 'ANCIENT ENERGY'
claims.note: Age metaphor for >= 4e4 yr; the tag says the energy, not the light or the photo, is ancient.

claims.claim: Card 8: ISS orbital sunrise photo, cut-out hand, 'LAST 8 MINUTES' then 'THE TRIP TO YOU'
claims.note: As claim 7.

claims.claim: Title: The energy in sunlight took at least tens of thousands of years to get out of the Sun
claims.note: Lowest cited figure 40,000 yr (SVS: 'Over tens of thousands of years'); MS92 1.7e5; MSFC ~1e6. 'At least' is exactly the bound all three support.

claims.claim: Caption: Sunlight reaches you about eight minutes after leaving the Sun.
claims.note: 8.1-8.4 min; 'about' is accurate.

claims.claim: Caption: The energy it carries spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out.
claims.note: Same wording as the spoken hook.

claims.claim: Description: Sunlight reaches you about eight minutes after leaving the Sun's surface.
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth 488-505 s.

claims.claim: Description: But the energy it carries spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out.
claims.note: Same as the hook.

claims.claim: Description: Estimates include about 40,000 years (NASA SVS), 170,000 (Mitalas & Sills 1992) and about a million (NASA Marshall).
claims.note: SVS 'Over the course of 40,000 years'; MS92 't_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr' (abstract and Sec. 3); MSFC 'about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Attributions and figures match. MS92 and MSFC time the trip to the convection-zone base rather than the surface; MS92 argues that is the diffusion time scale of the Sun since convective crossing is 'very much shorter', and the next sentence of the description says so, so 'getting out' is a fair gloss.

claims.claim: Description: The slow part is diffusing out through the Sun's dense interior; in the outer 30%, convection carries it up quickly.
claims.note: MSFC: 'they bounce so many times through this dense material'; convection zone 'the outermost 30%'; 'These convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface.' MS92: convective crossing time 'very much shorter' than the diffusion time.

claims.claim: Description: It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: MSFC: 'leaves the surface as visible light'.
